sections.overview: The Long-tailed Duck is a circumpolar Arctic breeder and a strongly migratory sea duck, wintering on northern marine coasts.
sections.identification: The adult male’s exceptionally long central tail feathers give the species its English name; plumage changes markedly through the year.
sections.habitat: It nests on Arctic tundra near freshwater pools and lakes, but spends winter at sea, often offshore or in sheltered coastal waters.
sections.diet: It dives for marine invertebrates, especially crustaceans and molluscs, with fish and freshwater prey also taken.
sections.behavior: It is a capable deep diver and forms large, social feeding and resting flocks outside the breeding season.
sections.reproduction: The female lays in a concealed ground nest near water; the male leaves after incubation begins, and young are mobile soon after hatching.
sections.ecology: Its seasonal shift from tundra wetlands to marine feeding grounds links Arctic freshwater breeding habitat with coastal food webs.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists it as Vulnerable after a severe decline in Baltic wintering numbers, while trends elsewhere remain less certain.
